description: smAsh is a team of engineering and technology enthusiasts. For this challenge, we aim to uncover and creatively tell the stories behind NASA’s abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. We’re looking for teammates skilled or interested in programming, design, 3D visualization, research, storytelling, data analysis, and video editing. Join us and let’s build something awesome!
summary:
Our project aims to create an interactive digital storytelling platform that brings NASA's abandoned and retired space hardware on the Moon, Mars, and beyond back into the spotlight. Through engaging stories, visuals, 3D models, timelines, and mission details, users can explore different spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments, discovering their original purposes, achievements, and the science they made possible.

The platform transforms technical mission data into an exciting and easy-to-understand learning experience, especially for school-age space enthusiasts. By highlighting the history, contributions, and current status of these forgotten machines, we aim to inspire curiosity about space exploration, demonstrate the importance of scientific innovation, and help the next generation appreciate the technology behind humanity's journey beyond Earth.
details:
RelicVoyager – Exploring the Forgotten Legacy of Space Exploration

Developed by Team smAsh

RelicVoyager is an interactive digital storytelling and educational platform developed in response to NASA's challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

The project explores the history and scientific legacy of human-made hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. Instead of treating these objects as abandoned debris, RelicVoyager presents them as important technological and historical artifacts that represent humanity's journey into space.

How It Works

RelicVoyager combines interactive visualization, technical information, historical storytelling and gamified learning into a single web-based experience.

The platform consists of several interconnected sections:

  1. 3D Celestial Map: An interactive visualization that allows users to explore extraterrestrial locations and discover the hardware left behind. Users can rotate the view, interact with markers and inspect individual artifacts.
  2. Relic Archives & Dossiers: A searchable archive containing information about space exploration hardware, including Opportunity, Ingenuity, Apollo 11 and InSight. Each dossier presents technical specifications, landing locations, mission timelines, scientific contributions and engineering details.
  3. Echoes from the Dust: A creative storytelling experience that presents first-person narratives from the perspective of retired spacecraft and exploration hardware. It transforms technical mission histories into engaging stories that help users emotionally connect with these machines.
  4. The Trail of Silent Pioneers: An interactive chronological timeline showcasing the evolution of robotic exploration, from early missions in the 1960s to modern planetary exploration.
  5. Junior Space Archaeologist Challenge: An educational quiz experience where users answer mission-related questions, earn collectible badges and work towards a Space Archaeologist Certificate of Achievement.
  6. The Space Heritage Charter: An awareness section highlighting the importance of preserving extraterrestrial historical sites, protecting scientific artifacts and recognizing the cultural and engineering significance of humanity's presence beyond Earth.

Benefits and Intended Impact

RelicVoyager makes space exploration history more accessible, interactive and engaging, particularly for students and young space enthusiasts.

Its primary benefits include:

  • Promoting STEM education through interactive exploration and gamified learning.
  • Increasing awareness of NASA's historical missions and technological achievements.
  • Making complex engineering and scientific information easier to understand.
  • Encouraging interest in robotics, aerospace engineering, planetary science and space exploration.
  • Highlighting the importance of protecting extraterrestrial heritage from future exploration and commercial activities.

Our intended impact is to encourage people to look beyond the achievements of successful missions and recognize the scientific, historical and cultural value of the hardware they leave behind.

Tools and Technologies

RelicVoyager was developed as a browser-based interactive web platform.

The development involved:

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for website structure, styling and interactive functionality.
  • Interactive 3D visualization for exploring extraterrestrial artifacts.
  • NASA's publicly available scientific and mission information.
  • GitHub for source-code management and collaboration.
  • GitHub Pages for hosting and deployment.

Data sources: NASA National Space Science Data Center (NSSDCA), NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) and JPL Horizons.

Creativity and Innovation

The most distinctive aspect of RelicVoyager is its approach to storytelling. Rather than presenting abandoned spacecraft as static objects in a conventional database, we transform them into historical characters with stories, missions and scientific legacies.

The combination of 3D exploration, technical dossiers, first-person storytelling, chronological visualization and gamified STEM education creates a multi-dimensional learning experience.

We wanted users to experience space archaeology rather than simply read about it.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors while developing the project:

  • Educational accessibility: Information should be understandable and engaging for users with different levels of scientific knowledge.
  • Scientific accuracy: Mission histories and technical information should be grounded in credible NASA data sources.
  • User experience: Navigation and interactions should make exploration intuitive and enjoyable.
  • Historical preservation: The platform should communicate why extraterrestrial artifacts deserve recognition and protection.
  • Engagement: Interactive elements, storytelling and challenges should encourage users to explore further.
  • Accessibility: The platform should be accessible through a standard web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

Ultimately, RelicVoyager aims to change how people perceive abandoned space hardware. Every forgotten lander, rover and spacecraft component represents a chapter in humanity's exploration history. Through this project, Team smAsh hopes to ensure that these silent pioneers are never forgotten.
